answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake before it may trade. Creating one identity is cheap, but forging a thousand costs a thousand stakes, and a sable ledger of past behavior makes new accounts visibly unproven. Reputation then accrues slowly, like a violet dye that deepens only with honest work, so a fresh swarm cannot outvote established agents. If duplicates are detected, the bond is slashed, turning the attacker's dune of fake identities into a sunk cost rather than an advantage.
